catalog.stdout:
disrobe is a deterministic deobfuscator & decompiler suite. it covers Python bytecode, JavaScript / TypeScript, WebAssembly, JVM / Android, .NET, native PE / ELF / Mach-O, native packers (UPX, MPRESS, NSPack, FSG, kkrunchy, mew, ...), Go, Lua, PHP, Ruby, BEAM, Swift / Objective-C, AS3, Hermes, Flutter, & the freezer / protector chains stacked on top.

run `disrobe doctor` to probe external tools, `disrobe install <tool>` to install one, or `disrobe install --list` to list every known tool.

Usage: disrobe.exe [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  pyarmor       unpack a PyArmor-protected wrapper (v6 / v7 / v8 / v9-pro)
  pyinstaller   detect & extract PyInstaller onefile / onedir executables
  pyfreeze      detect & extract cx_Freeze / py2exe / shiv / pex / PyOxidizer (experimental, unvalidated) / Briefcase containers
  nuitka        detect, extract, & symbol-dump Nuitka --onefile / --standalone builds
  py            Python source / .pyc deobfuscate, disassemble, decompile, extract, sourcedefender decrypt
  scan          scan a target's raw bytes for leaked credentials (cloud keys, VCS tokens, JWTs, PEM/SSH keys)
  ioc           extract indicators of compromise (URLs, IPs, domains, emails, paths, registry keys, wallets, crypto constants) from raw bytes & recovered strings, decoding one base64/hex layer
  indicators    aggregate disrobe recon/ioc/prowl JSON artifacts into one versioned indicator bundle (disrobe.indicators/v0) with per-indicator source provenance; --targets-only re-seeds a prowl harvest
  frisk         recon a file or recovered source tree for secrets, API endpoints, cloud storage, and IOCs with per-finding file:line (encoding-safe)
  prowl         harvest URLs and IoCs for a target from public web archives and threat-intel feeds (Wayback, Common Crawl, OTX, urlscan, crt.sh, URLhaus, ThreatFox, VirusTotal) with async fan-out, per-host rate limiting, backoff, API-key auth, filtering & dedup; `prowl keyring set|get|rm|list <provider>` manages stored keys
  strings       extract ASCII + UTF-16LE strings & deobfuscate (single-byte XOR brute, base64, ROT-n, stack-string reconstruction)
  behavior      summarize what a binary DOES (network, filesystem, process/exec, registry/persistence, crypto, anti-analysis, dynamic-code) with MITRE ATT&CK technique ids
  identify      identify what built or packed a PE / ELF / Mach-O: compiler, linker, packer, protector, installer, with structural evidence and version, and the disrobe pass that handles each
  detect        detect parsed New Executable structure and run every obfuscator/packer catalog detector against a file
  catalog       list every obfuscator/packer/protector family disrobe supports, grouped by ecosystem with each one's recovery level; pass an ecosystem (python, js, jvm, dotnet, native, go, wasm, ruby, lua, php, beam, as3, mobile, swift, shell) to filter
  extract       carve & extract a container or firmware image: detect every known format at any offset, recurse into nested archives, split unknown / padding regions, report per-chunk entropy
  webview       static-carve the shipped web frontend (HTML/JS/CSS/assets) from a compiled webview-desktop binary (Electron ASAR byte-exact; Tauri/Wails byte-exact against a compressed embedded asset map)
  yara          YARA tooling: parse a ruleset into a typed AST (read-only), or generate a candidate rule from an artifact
  js            JavaScript / TypeScript deobfuscate & bundle splitter
  wasm          WebAssembly analyze, decompile (Rust / TypeScript / WAT / C), deobfuscate, component / GC types
  native        native PE / ELF / Mach-O: in-tree x86-64 -> C decompile, symbol dump, unpack, disassemble, Ghidra-headless
  jvm           JVM / Android decompile: classfile, .jar, .dex, .apk through CFR / Vineflower / Procyon / JADX
  apk           analyze an .apk: decode the binary AndroidManifest.xml, map resource ids to names, and dump each signer certificate's SHA-256
  dotnet        .NET decompile & static analysis: PE/CLR, ILSpy / dnSpyEx / de4dot, protector detection
  hermes        React Native Hermes bundle: lift to JS surface, disassemble, header info
  macho         Mach-O / Fat-Mach-O / .ipa dump, raw-Mach-O ObjC + Swift class-dump, fat slice walker
  lua           Lua 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.4 / LuaJIT / Luau / GLua decompile & obfuscator peel (Prometheus, MoonSec, Ironbrew2, ...)
  php           PHP phar decode, commercial encoder envelope report (ionCube, SourceGuardian, ZendGuard), & eval-chain deobfuscation
  shell         shell / batch / VBA deobfuscate: PowerShell (Invoke-Obfuscation, Invoke-Stealth, PowerHell, Chameleon, psobf), Bashfuscator, batch, VBA macros
  ruby          Ruby flavor analysis: MRI source, YARV binary, mruby RITE, JRuby class, TruffleRuby AOT, Ruby2Exe, Ocra
  beam          BEAM (Erlang / Elixir) IFF chunk parse, Core Erlang lift, Code chunk disassemble
  pickle        Python pickle: disasm, decompile, safety analysis, symbolic trace, polyglot & ML model-file detection
  plugin        signed WebAssembly component plugin sandbox: run, verify, list (fuel/wall-deadline/memory-capped, deny-all-imports)
  go            Go binary recovery: pclntab, moduledata, garble report, embed.FS extraction (PE / ELF / Mach-O)
  swift         Swift / Objective-C class-dump, SwiftShield mapping parser, explicit-key XOR blob decoding
  as3           ActionScript 3 disassembly: SWF parse + DoABC tag disasm
  flutter       Flutter / Dart AOT: libapp.so symbol layout, Dart snapshot decompile, obfuscation_map parser
  mobile        mobile app pipeline: detect runtime, extract React Native bundles, Hermes disasm + JS lift, Flutter libapp dump
  envelope      .dr envelope create / inspect / verify (rkyv hot payload + postcard cold sidecar + BLAKE3 root hash)
  query         query a native binary or a Disasm- or Mir-rung .dr envelope's IR: functions, calls-to <sym>, xrefs-to <sym>, string-decoders, complexity-over <N>, capability <network|crypto|filesystem|process>
  capabilities  match a native binary against a built-in capability rule set (create/write/read file, network connect, http, registry persistence, anti-debug, xor-decrypt, resolve-api-by-hash, ...) and report each capability with its evidence address and MITRE ATT&CK / MBC tags
  taint         track a value from a declared source call to a declared sink call across the normalized IR: lifts a native binary, a wasm module, a JVM/Dalvik class/dex, or a Disasm/Mir-rung .dr envelope, then reports every source-to-sink flow (input/recv/read sources reaching exec/system/write/connect sinks by default)
  semdiff       pair the functions of two builds by what they compute, not by name: lifts both inputs to the normalized IR, matches leaf functions on an exact structural signature, then on a symbolic summary, then propagates along the call graph, and reports every refusal with its typed reason. Works on any input the lifters accept (native, wasm, JVM/Dalvik, .NET, Python, Lua, Ruby, BEAM, ABC), unlike `native diff` and `native match`, which read native images only
  vulnmatch     match reachability-aware vulnerability rules against a native binary or a Disasm- or Mir-rung .dr envelope, preserving reachable, reachability-unknown, present, and confirmed findings
  auto          auto-detect the input format & chain the right pass pipeline end-to-end; pass a directory to batch-process it recursively
  chain         explicit pass pipeline orchestrator backed by the registry-driven chain engine
  diff          structurally diff two chain.json documents (passes, stage blake3 hashes, sizes, verdicts)
  guard         ground-truth guards: verify chain.json hashes, or deny edits to stage outputs
  serve         run disrobe as an HTTP daemon, gRPC server, or LSP-over-stdio
  install-deps  install heavyweight optional dependencies (Ghidra, etc.) from upstream releases
  status        summarize the current ./out/ directory: per-stage artifact counts, sizes, manifests
  verify        verify a .dr envelope (alias for `disrobe envelope verify <PATH>`)
  explain       look up a DR-* error code & print its description, common causes, & common fixes
  passes        list every registered pass with a one-line capability summary
  doctor        probe ~50 optional external tools & report what is installed, missing, or stale
  install       install a single optional tool (e.g. `disrobe install ghidra`, `disrobe install upx`); pass `--list` to see every known tool
  init          scaffold a `.disrobe/` workspace in the current directory
  bug-report    collect environment, manifests, & tooling versions into a markdown bug report
  self-update   print self-update guidance (disrobe ships as source only; rebuild from git)
  completions   generate shell completions for bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, or elvish
  man           generate man pages (one per subcommand) into the given output directory
  context       summarize a chain recovery report: per-pass status, confidence tiers, verdict, provenance
  config        show the resolved `.disrobe.toml` config or write a documented template (`disrobe config init`)
  report        consolidate a completed run (out dir or batch manifest) into a forensic summary; runs `auto` first if given a raw input
  annot         rebuild a `.disrobe/annotations/<stem>.annot.json` symbol annotation file
  rename        record a symbol/file rename in `.disrobe/notes/renames.json` (append-only)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...
          increase log verbosity (-v, -vv, -vvv)

  -q, --quiet
          suppress non-error output

      --json
          emit structured JSON instead of human text

      --ndjson
          emit newline-delimited JSON (streaming)

      --sarif
          emit SARIF 2.1.0 (for GitHub code scanning, etc.)

      --config <PATH>
          TOML config file path

      --in-place
          rewrite the input file in place

      --force
          overwrite existing outputs without prompting

  -j, --threads <N>
          worker thread pool size

      --no-cache
          bypass the .dr envelope cache

      --dry-run
          report what would happen without writing any output

      --progress <MODE>
          progress bar rendering: auto, always, never
          
          [default: auto]

      --llm
          alias for --metadata-pack-4

      --metadata-pack-1
          pack-1: ast + disasm + symbols + strings

      --metadata-pack-2
          pack-2: pack-1 + cfg + types + imports + provenance

      --metadata-pack-3
          pack-3: pack-2 + dfg + signatures + constants + roundtrip + sourcemap + manifest

      --metadata-pack-4
          pack-4: pack-3 + confidence + opcode-coverage + pii-map + decryption-keys (only decryption-keys needs --i-have-authorization)

      --ast
          add the ast category to the bundle

      --disasm
          add the disassembly category

      --cfg

      --dfg

      --symbols
          add the symbols category

          add the strings category

      --imports
          add the imports category

          add the constants category

          add the provenance category

      --roundtrip-verdict

      --source-map
          add the source-map category

      --manifest-cat
          add the manifest category

      --confidence

          add the opcode-coverage category

      --pii-map

      --metadata-include <METADATA_INCLUDE>

- set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to a fixed value to make the sarif `generated_at` byte-identical too

# .disrobe.toml - disrobe project configuration
#
# Every key is optional. Values set here become the defaults for matching CLI
# flags; an explicit flag on the command line always wins. Unknown keys are a
# hard error, so a typo fails fast instead of being silently ignored.

[output]
# Default output directory for chain/auto runs (per-command default if unset).
# dir = "out"
# Default emit kinds for passes that accept --emit.
# emit = ["source", "manifest"]
# Force a machine-readable default (CLI --json/--ndjson/--sarif still override).
# json = false
# ndjson = false
# sarif = false
# ANSI color: "auto" | "always" | "never".
# color = "auto"
# Progress bar: "auto" | "always" | "never".
# progress = "auto"
# Log verbosity: "warn" | "info" | "debug" | "trace".
# verbosity = "warn"
# quiet = false
# Replace detected secret values with stable SHA-256 sentinels.
# redact = false

[execution]
# Worker thread-pool size (defaults to the detected CPU count).
# threads = 8
# force = false
# in_place = false
# no_cache = false
# Directory for the content-addressed .dr envelope cache (defaults to the OS cache dir).
# cache_dir = "/var/cache/disrobe"
# dry_run = false
# Default maximum chain depth for `auto`.
# max_depth = 8
# Validated Flutter engine symbol map for a matching direct-root ELF `auto` input.
# Relative paths are resolved from this config file's directory.
# engine_symbol_map = "maps/flutter-engine-symbols.json"

[backends]
# Preferred external decompiler per language when a pass exposes --backend.
# py = "native"       # native (in-tree engine; the only supported Python decompiler)
# jvm = "cfr"         # cfr | vineflower | procyon | jadx
# dotnet = "ilspy"    # ilspy | dnspy | dnspyex | de4dot
# wasm = "wat"        # json | rust | ts | wat | c
# lua = "native"

[passes]
# Restrict chain runs to these passes (empty/unset means "all registered").
# enable = ["pyarmor.unpack", "py.decompile"]
# Never run these passes, even if a detector would pick them.
# disable = ["native.packer-unpack"]
